clue.text: Shocking word repeated in error

indicators.note: repeated tells us to write the exclamation twice in a row

parts.note: boo is the word shouted to startle or shock someone

explanation.surface: Someone blurts out a startling expletive twice in a row, and it was a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A childish or informal word for a silly mistake or blunder, synonym of error.

clue.text: Just over line in big city

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: in puts the line letter inside the city abbreviation

parts.note: NY, New York, is the big city

explanation.surface: Something barely crosses a line in a large city.
explanation.definitionFit: Only and just both mean merely or no more than.

clue.text: Britain's first non-resident bird

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of Britain's

parts.note: rambling means wandering about, not staying put

explanation.surface: Britain's first migratory bird is noted.
explanation.definitionFit: The brambling is a finch, a species of bird that winters in Britain.

clue.text: God lost heart to goddess

indicators.note: heart takes the central letters of the word lost

parts.note: Iris is the Greek goddess of the rainbow

explanation.surface: A god loses his heart to a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the Egyptian myth of a dismembered god restored by his consort; 'lost' is fodder, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris is the Egyptian deity of the underworld and the dead.

clue.text: Painter's last to board plane and he's first to touch up picture

indicators.note: to board means to get on, so one letter goes inside the aircraft word

parts.note: an Airbus is a make of passenger plane

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word Painter's
first picks the opening letter of the word he's

explanation.surface: An artist is the last aboard an aircraft, and someone else is first to retouch a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To airbrush a photograph is to retouch it with a spray tool, removing blemishes.

clue.text: Rocking chairs before low life?

indicators.note: rocking shakes the following words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rocking chairs come before a lowly existence.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as a phrase: 'Life is just a bowl of cherries' is the song line.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says life is pleasant and carefree, from a well-known song title.

clue.text: Let out from fields, having cut grass

indicators.note: having cut means the fields word slices into the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
leas are meadows or fields

explanation.surface: Something is let out of the fields after the grass is mown.
explanation.definitionFit: Released means freed or let go, as in let out of prison.

clue.text: Dexter's prerogative

definitions.meaning: dexter is the heraldic word for the ...-hand side, so dexter is equivalent to ...
a prerogative is an entitlement, something one is due

explanation.definitionFit: Dexter means right-handed in Latin, and a prerogative is a privilege or entitlement.

clue.text: Poor actor needs play

indicators.note: play means the letters are toyed with and moved around

explanation.surface: An underperforming actor needs a part in a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-rate means of inferior quality, so poor or mediocre.

clue.text: Animal lacking tail that's taken home by old star

indicators.note: lacking tail means the animal's final letter is dropped

parts.note: an alpaca is a South American woolly animal
in means at home

explanation.surface: An old film star takes home a tailless animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Pacino is a famous American film actor, an example of a movie star.

clue.text: What's left, say, in fluid clay

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the rearranged letters
fluid means flowing and shapeless, so the letters of clay are reshaped

parts.note: eg (for example) is what say means in 'say, a dog'

explanation.surface: Something remains, for instance, in wet clay.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is something bequeathed or left behind by a person after death.

clue.text: Scented oil bad in ship, not good

indicators.note: in puts the word for bad inside the shortened vessel
not good means the letter for good is taken out

parts.note: a brigantine is a two-masted sailing ship
ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A perfumed oil has gone off aboard a vessel and is no good.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliantine is a perfumed hair oil used to make hair glossy.

clue.text: Bad habit causing tension

definitions.meaning: chewing one's fingernails is a common nervous vice
a tense, suspenseful match or film keeps you on edge

explanation.definitionFit: The compound means both chewing the fingernails and nerve-racking, as in a suspenseful finish.

clue.text: Make heavy demands on island transport

parts.note: to tax someone is to strain or burden them

explanation.surface: An island's transport system is put under heavy strain.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a hired car, a form of transport for passengers.

clue.text: Fine tool for gardener turning over a plant

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

indicators.note: over here means placed over, enclosing the letter a
turning means the gardening tool's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a trowel is a small hand tool used by gardeners

explanation.surface: A good gardening tool is used to turn over a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleawort is the name of a wild plant once used against fleas.

clue.text: Somewhere in London pants go down without ever going up

indicators.note: without means outside, so the shuffled letters surround the reversed word
pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are a mess
going up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: Somewhere in London pants are pulled down but never pulled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' (British slang for rubbish) is the anagram signal on GO DOWN; E'ER is a poetic spelling, and 'without' means outside. Wood Green is a district of north London.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood Green is a district in the north London borough of Haringey.

clue.text: Penny drops — it concealed hidden dangers

indicators.note: concealed means the small word is tucked inside the others

parts.note: falls means drops, as rain falls

explanation.surface: A coin drops, hiding dangers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitfalls are unsuspected dangers or traps, originally covered pits.

clue.text: Shot with silent movie star in slow motion

parts.note: a slug is a bullet, or a shot of spirits
Lillian Gish was a star of silent films

explanation.surface: A gunshot and a silent film actress appear in a slow-motion sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluggish means moving slowly and lethargically, as if slowed down.

clue.text: Strong language in set-to at home

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Swearing breaks out during a domestic row.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a swear word, an example of strong language.

clue.text: Capital investment originally in Hardy novel

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the rearranged name
novel means new, so the letters of Hardy take a new form
originally picks the first letter of investment

explanation.surface: Money is invested in a Thomas Hardy novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Riyadh is the capital city of Saudi Arabia.

clue.text: Persuasive speech of royalist working on a farm?

parts.note: a pitch is a persuasive sales talk
a royalist is for the king, on the monarch's side

explanation.surface: A supporter of the crown is making a sales speech while doing farm work.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: pitchforking hay is one kind of farm work.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitchforking means tossing hay with a long-handled fork, typical farm labour.

clue.text: Pachelbel's work as a clergyman?

definitions.meaning: Pachelbel's best-known piece is the ... in D
a cathedral clergyman with a set office

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a musical form using imitative voices, and a cathedral cleric.

clue.text: Black and white lamb starts to cry

indicators.note: starts picks the first letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A black-and-white lamb begins to cry.
explanation.definitionFit: To bawl is to cry loudly, a synonym for wail.

clue.text: First person taken in by isolated Labour leader — Blair

indicators.note: taken in by means placed inside the next word

parts.note: lone means isolated or solitary
I is the first person singular pronoun

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of Labour

explanation.surface: Someone is taken in by a lonely Labour Party leader called Blair.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at Tony Blair the Labour prime minister; the definition is the forename of Lionel Blair, an English entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lionel Blair was a British dancer and television presenter, so his first name fits.

clue.text: One-time setting for Greek god? Possibly

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: setting for means the time word surrounds the god like a jewel's setting

parts.note: a day is a period of time
Ares is the Greek god of war

explanation.surface: A question asks whether there was once a backdrop for a Greek deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a hedging expression of supposition meaning perhaps.

clue.text: Having abandoned Saigon, Midwest is very worried

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot

parts.note: read as mid-west: the middle letters of the word west

explanation.surface: Someone who has left Saigon for the American Midwest is very anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise is to worry intensely, so the third-person form means is distressed.

clue.text: Cope with composer in recital

indicators.note: in recital means spoken out, so we go by how the name sounds

parts.note: Handel was a German-British baroque composer

explanation.surface: A performer copes with a composer's work during a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle a situation is to manage it or deal with it.
